q: 1. Among the following, which gas is the main cause of depletion of ozone layer?
explain: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine atoms when broken down by UV radiation, which then catalyze the destruction of ozone molecules.

q: 2. Kyoto Protocol was ratified by Nepal --------
explain: Nepal ratified the Kyoto Protocol on September 16, 2005.

q: 3. Where the UN Climate Change Conference COP 28 held?
explain: COP 28 was hosted by the United Arab Emirates in Dubai in late 2023.

q: 4. Which of the following is not major green house gas?
explain: Nitrogen (N2) makes up 78% of the atmosphere but is not a greenhouse gas because its diatomic molecules do not absorb infrared radiation.

q: 5. Who was the first person to experiment scientifically about the greenhouse effects?
explain: Eunice Newton Foote (1856) and John Tyndall (1859) both independently discovered and experimented on the heat-trapping properties of CO2.
The Kyoto Protocol is an international agreement linked to the UNFCCC, specifically aimed at fighting global warming and climate change.

q: 7. When was the first Nepal national wetland Policy issued by the Government?
explain: The first National Wetland Policy of Nepal was formulated in 2053 B.S. (1996) to manage wetland resources sustainably.

q: 8. In which of the following district of Nepal, biodiversity information centre is being established?
explain: A key Biodiversity Information Centre is established at Kasara, Chitwan, within the Chitwan National Park.

q: 9. Which of the following does not fall into category of biodiversity?
explain: Biodiversity typically includes genetic (hereditary), species, and ecosystem (environmental) diversity. 'Climate diversity' describes weather patterns, not biological variety.

q: 10. The largest ecosystem of the earth is --------
explain: The hydrosphere (oceans, seas, lakes) covers about 71% of the Earth's surface, making it the largest ecosystem.

q: 11. What is the theme of World Biodiversity Day 2024 A.D.?
explain: The theme for International Day for Biological Diversity 2024 is 'Be part of the Plan'.

q: 12. How many places of Nepal have been declared wetland now?
explain: As per current Ramsar Convention records, Nepal has 10 sites designated as Wetlands of International Importance.

q: 13. How many kinds of ecosystem are found in Nepal?
explain: The 1988 Biodiversity Strategy identified 118 distinct ecosystems in Nepal across its various physiographic zones.

q: 14. The richest country in the world presented by mongabay.com -2021 in terms of Bio-diversity is
explain: Brazil is consistently ranked as the most biodiverse country in the world due to the Amazon rainforest.

q: 15. Where is the bio-diversity information centre established?
explain: As mentioned in question 76, the centre is located in Chitwan.

q: 16. Which of the following among given richest country is richest in the field of Biodiversity?
explain: Among the options provided, Indonesia holds the highest biodiversity due to its tropical archipelagic nature.

q: 17. According to mongabay.com report-2023, Nepal ranked -------- in the world in term of Biodiversity.
explain: In the Global Biodiversity Index (2023), Nepal is ranked 49th out of nearly 200 countries.

q: 18. 'Bio-diversity Day' is celebrated every year on --------
explain: The United Nations has proclaimed May 22 as the International Day for Biological Diversity.

q: 19. Which of the following component is not related with bio - diversity?
explain: Biodiversity consists of genetic, species, and ecosystem levels. Geographic diversity refers to landforms, not biological variety.
